Web Push Countly Implementation




What the SDK does on its own: once push_vapid_public_key is set, every load re-registers the subscription token if the browser has already granted notification permission, and notification clicks are recorded as [CLY]_push_action without any code here. The button below is only needed for the very first opt-in, because browsers refuse a permission prompt that does not come from a user gesture. Pass push_auto_register: false to turn the automatic part off.

How to test: Serve this repo over HTTPS, or over HTTP from localhost, so the /countly_sw.js path is reachable from the page. Service workers and the Push API need a secure context: file:// and plain-HTTP LAN or hosted origins are both refused, only loopback is exempt. Replace app_key, url and push_vapid_public_key above. Click "Enable Push Notifications" and accept the browser prompt (in Edge the prompt is a bell icon at the right end of the address bar, not a popup) — the SDK will queue a token_session request containing the web_token JSON. To simulate a click-through, open DevTools → Application → Service Workers and use the "Push" button of the countly_sw.js worker, whose scope is /countly-push/, to inject a payload such as {"title":"Hi","message":"Test","c":{"i":"507f1f77bcf86cd799439011"}}. The i value must be a 24-character message id: the server drops [CLY]_push_action events whose id has any other length. Pressing "Disable" is remembered across reloads; only "Enable" subscribes again.

Seeing what happens: with debug: true the SDK registers the worker as /countly_sw.js?cly_debug=1, so the worker narrates every push, click and close in its own console (DevTools → Application → Service Workers → Inspect) and forwards the same lines to this page, where they appear as [SW]. The push_notification_listener above writes each notification event below.
